findings.title: Mocked authentication is configured for production
findings.remediation: Configure a production authentication strategy, for example in package.json: `"cds": { "requires": { "[production]": { "auth": "xsuaa" } } }` (or `"ias"`), bind the app to an XSUAA or IAS instance, and keep `mocked` and its users under `[development]` only. Verify the result with `cds env get requires.auth --profile production`.

findings.title: Service is open to everyone
findings.remediation: Restrict the service with `@requires`, for example `service AdminService @(requires: 'admin') { ... }`, using a role that xs-security.json defines as a scope and role template, and add `@restrict` rules on entities or actions that need finer control (`@restrict: [{ grant: 'READ', to: 'viewer' }]`). Mark data that must never be changed through the service with `@readonly`. A service that is only consumed in-process should declare `@protocol: 'none'`. If the service must stay open to every authenticated user, say so explicitly with `@requires: 'authenticated-user'`. When the production profile sets `restrict_all_services: false` or a development authentication strategy, remove that as well, since it lets unauthenticated callers in.

findings.title: Seed data column 6 contains payment card numbers
findings.remediation: Remove the real values from the CSV file: replace card numbers and IBANs with clearly synthetic, masked values that fail the format checks (for example `****-****-****-1111`), leave secret columns empty, or drop the column from the seed file altogether. Secrets belong in a service binding or a credential store, never in seed data. Keep `db/data` for configuration data and code lists that must reach production; test data belongs in `test/data`, which CAP loads in development only. If the values are real, treat them as exposed: rotate the secrets and remove the file from the repository history as well, since deleting it in a new commit leaves it in every clone.

findings.title: CSRF protection is disabled on an authenticated approuter route
findings.remediation: Remove `"csrfProtection": false` from the route in xs-app.json (the default is `true`), so the application router answers 403 to every request other than GET and HEAD (PUT, POST, PATCH, DELETE, ...) that carries no valid `x-csrf-token` header. Clients obtain the token with a GET or HEAD request that sends `x-csrf-token: fetch`; the SAPUI5 OData models and the CAP Fiori preview do this on their own. If the route only ever serves GET and HEAD, CSRF protection costs nothing, so there is no reason to switch it off. If `cds add app-frontend` generated the route, set the flag back to `true` after generating and let the frontend fetch the token.

findings.title: Approuter route forwards requests without authentication
findings.remediation: Remove `authenticationType: none` from the route, or set it to `xsuaa` (or `ias` when the approuter is bound to Identity Authentication), so the approuter forwards only requests with a valid session and passes the user token to the backend. Keep `none` only for routes that serve public static content from a `localDir` or the UI5 CDN, and for the logout page. If the destination must stay reachable without a login, make sure the backend enforces its own authentication and does not trust the approuter to have done it.

findings.title: Audit logging plugin is listed under devDependencies only, so it is inactive in production
findings.remediation: Annotate the entities that hold personal data with `@PersonalData` (`EntitySemantics` and `DataSubjectRole` on the entity; `FieldSemantics`, `IsPotentiallyPersonal` or `IsPotentiallySensitive` on the elements), then move `@cap-js/audit-logging` from `devDependencies` to `dependencies`: with `NODE_ENV=production` cds loads plugins from `dependencies` only, so the deployed app runs without audit logging. Make sure an SAP Audit Log service instance (service `auditlog`, plan `premium`) is bound to the app. The plugin logs only entities annotated with `@PersonalData`, so keep those annotations complete. Verify with `cds env requires.audit-log --profile production`.

findings.title: Audit logging is installed but no audit log service is bound
findings.remediation: Add an SAP Audit Log service instance to the MTA descriptor and require it from the server module: a resource of type `org.cloudfoundry.managed-service` with `service: auditlog` and `service-plan: premium` (what `cds add audit-logging` generates), or `org.cloudfoundry.existing-service` named after an instance created with `cf create-service auditlog premium <name>`; then list the resource under the module `requires`. The plugin finds the `audit-log-to-restv2` binding by its VCAP label `auditlog`; with Audit Log Service NG (`audit-log-to-alsng`) the binding must be named `auditlog-ng`. Without a binding the audit log service cannot initialise in production and audit entries are not written. Verify with `cds env requires.audit-log --profile production` and `cf services`.

findings.title: Entity holds personal data without @PersonalData annotations
findings.remediation: Annotate the entity, preferably in a separate `db/data-privacy.cds` file: `annotate <Entity> with @PersonalData: { EntitySemantics: 'DataSubject', DataSubjectRole: '<Role>' }` for the entity that represents the person, or `EntitySemantics: 'DataSubjectDetails'` for an entity that belongs to one through an association; mark the key, or the association to the data subject, with `@PersonalData.FieldSemantics: 'DataSubjectID'`, each personal element with `@PersonalData.IsPotentiallyPersonal` and sensitive ones (salary, religion, card numbers) with `@PersonalData.IsPotentiallySensitive`. With the `@cap-js/audit-logging` plugin in place (see CAP_AUDITLOG_MISSING), changes of personal and reads of sensitive elements are then logged. The finding is inferred from element and entity names: if the elements are not personal data, rename them so they no longer look like it, or accept the finding.

findings.title: Role referenced in the CDS model has no scope in the XSUAA descriptor
findings.remediation: Add a scope `$XSAPPNAME.<role>` and a role template `<role>` with that scope in its `scope-references` to xs-security.json (or regenerate the file from the model with `cds compile srv --to xsuaa > xs-security.json`), update the xsuaa service instance and assign the role through a role collection. If the name in `@requires` or `@restrict` is a typo, fix the annotation so that it matches an existing scope. When roles are meant to come from Authorization Management Service policies, add `@sap/ams` and configure `cds.requires.auth: ams` for production.

findings.title: Deployment archive (.mtar) is not ignored by git
findings.remediation: Add `*.mtar` (or the build output folder, usually `mta_archives/`) to the root `.gitignore`. If the archive was already committed, stop tracking it with `git rm --cached <file>` and commit; if it reached a shared remote, treat every credential in its configuration files as exposed and rotate it, since removing the file does not remove it from the history. Build the archive in the pipeline with `mbt build` and deploy from there instead of keeping it next to the sources.

findings.title: SAPUI5 loaded from an external CDN without integrity protection
findings.remediation: Serve SAPUI5 through the approuter instead of a public CDN: route `resources/` to the `ui5` destination or to the HTML5 Application Repository, so the version is controlled by the landscape and does not change behind a deployed app. Where the CDN must stay, pin a specific version (`https://ui5.sap.com/1.120.3/resources/sap-ui-core.js`) rather than the evergreen or unversioned form, and add `integrity="sha384-…"` with `crossorigin="anonymous"` to the bootstrap script, knowing that they protect only the loader: the libraries it fetches at run time are still trusted blindly. Keep the pinned version inside maintenance, since the CDN removes versions one year after their end of maintenance.

findings.title: Mocked users carry passwords in the development configuration
findings.remediation: Delete the `password` values from the mocked users in `cds.requires.auth.users` and keep the `users` block under `[development]` only, so it never applies to production. A developer who needs a password-protected local login can define it in `.cdsrc-private.json`, which cds reads but which must stay out of version control. If any of these passwords was ever reused on another system, change it there.

findings.title: Scope is defined but no role template references it
findings.remediation: Reference the scope from a role template in the security descriptor, for example `"role-templates": [{ "name": "Admin", "scope-references": ["$XSAPPNAME.admin"] }]`, so it can be assigned through a role collection, or remove the scope. If another application is meant to call with it, grant it explicitly with `granted-apps` or `grant-as-authority-to-apps`. In a CAP project, regenerate the descriptor with `cds compile srv --to xsuaa` so scopes and role templates stay in step with the roles used in the CDS model.

rules.title: No deploy in the last 12 months
rules.description: The current droplet was staged more than 12 months ago. The app runs with the libraries, buildpack and runtime from that time, so fixes released since then are missing.

rules.title: Mocked authentication is configured for production
rules.description: The effective CAP configuration for the production profile uses a development authentication strategy (mocked, dummy or basic). With mocked, the pre-defined mock users shipped with @sap/cds (one of them an admin) and any other login are accepted unless the project overrides them; basic accepts the users listed in the project files; dummy accepts every request and disables @requires and @restrict.

rules.title: Mocked users carry passwords in the project configuration
rules.description: Mocked CAP users are defined with a password in a project configuration file (package.json or .cdsrc). Passwords in source files travel with every clone and are easy to reuse against other systems.

rules.title: Personal data is modelled but audit logging is not set up
rules.description: The CDS model holds personal data, but neither @cap-js/audit-logging nor an audit-log configuration is present, so reads and changes of personal data are not logged.

rules.title: Audit logging is installed but no audit log service is bound
rules.description: The project depends on @cap-js/audit-logging, but the MTA descriptor binds no audit log service, so the plugin cannot connect to an audit log service in production and personal-data accesses fail or go unlogged.

rules.title: Entity holds personal data without @PersonalData annotations
rules.description: An entity has fields that look like personal data (names, contact details, identifiers) but no @PersonalData annotation, so CAP cannot log access to it or apply its data-privacy features.

rules.title: Service is open to every authenticated user
rules.description: A CDS service declares no @requires or @restrict on the service, its entities or its actions. Every authenticated user, or everyone when authentication is mocked, can read and, unless its entities are read-only, change its data.

rules.title: Role referenced in the CDS model has no scope in the XSUAA descriptor
rules.description: A role named in @requires or @restrict has no matching scope in the XSUAA security descriptor, so nobody can be granted it: the restriction either locks everyone out or is bypassed by a misspelt role elsewhere.

rules.title: Scope is defined but no role template references it
rules.description: A scope in the XSUAA security descriptor is neither referenced by a role template nor granted to another application, so no role collection can ever carry it; such leftovers hide the real authorization model.

rules.title: Approuter route forwards requests without authentication
rules.description: An approuter route to a destination or service has authenticationType none, or the whole xs-app.json disables authentication, so backend endpoints are reachable without a login.

rules.title: CSRF protection is disabled on an authenticated approuter route
rules.description: A route to a destination sets csrfProtection to false while still requiring a login, so a malicious page can make the browser send state-changing requests with the user's session.

rules.title: Deployment archive (.mtar) is not ignored by git
rules.description: A built MTA archive lies in the project and no .gitignore pattern excludes it. Archives carry resolved dependencies and generated configuration, and they end up in the repository history.

rules.title: Seed data contains card numbers, IBANs or secrets
rules.description: A CSV seed file has a column whose name and values look like payment card numbers, IBANs or secrets (reported by column position, never by name). Seed data is deployed to every system and committed with the project.

rules.title: SAPUI5 loaded from an external CDN without integrity protection
rules.description: An HTML page bootstraps SAPUI5 from an external host without an integrity attribute, so the application trusts whatever that host serves, including an unpinned latest version.
